nm_north_left_face.blurb: The far left side of the Enchanted Tower near Datil, this face holds ten bolted sport lines on steep volcanic rock. Grades start at 5.11 and most sit in the 5.12 range, so it suits strong climbers rather than anyone warming up. The face is mostly shaded and does not pick up direct sun until mid to late afternoon in summer, which makes it a reasonable pick when the tower's sunnier faces are too hot. Expect wind at times. The base is a short walk along a trail that switchbacks up beside the tower from the camping area.

nm_mother_goose_wall.blurb: Mother Goose Wall is the friendliest section of the Enchanted Tower, near Datil at roughly 8,000 feet. About ten sport lines run from 5.6 up to the low 5.10s, with a handful of easier routes that make it the best spot at the tower for newer leaders and for moderate mileage. The climbing is vertical on generous holds and pockets, in a place otherwise known for steep, hard lines. Routes carry fairy tale names. The base is only a few minutes from the road.

nm_solar_asylum.blurb: Solar Asylum is a cliff of roughly a hundred feet above Hondo Creek in the John Dunn Bridge area near Taos. It is known for the hardest overhanging sport lines in the area, with a few trad and mixed options too; grades run from 5.10 into the 5.12s. The lower part is steep, blocky and featured, with a cleaner headwall of face and crack climbing above. The wall works on cold winter days because it takes sun, and in summer it stays shaded until late morning before the afternoon sun arrives.

nm_flake_n_bake.blurb: A small crag in lower La Cueva Canyon on the west side of the Sandia Mountains, above Albuquerque. Nearly all the climbing is trad, with a single top rope line, and the grades stay mostly in the 5.5 to 5.8 range, with just a few harder lines. The rock is good quality and low angle, which makes this a common place for a first trad lead or for teaching placement skills. Big boulders from past rockfall lie scattered around the base, and the way in follows the canyon stream.

nm_sun_devil_wall.blurb: Sun Devil Wall sits on the north side of Diablo Canyon outside Santa Fe, around the corner from Winter Wall and on the way toward Solar Cave. It holds about ten routes, mostly sport with a couple of trad lines, from 5.9 to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.11 range. Several are multi-pitch lines of two to four pitches, and many finish on the mesa where you can walk back to the car. The wall faces south and is warm on cold days; in early summer it shades over in the morning until about eleven. Wear a helmet, as loose rock is common in the canyon.

nm_left_end.blurb: Left End is the east end of Early Wall in Diablo Canyon, outside Santa Fe, and holds ten routes: seven sport and three trad. The grades lean hard, with most in the 5.11 to 5.12 range and only a few easier ones. Like the rest of the wall, it catches sun briefly early in the morning and sits in shade for the remainder of the day, so it suits warm weather better than cold days. Besides the main trail up to the wall, a faint cairned path along the left edge of the talus leads to the base.

nm_villain_wall.blurb: Villain Wall is a short wall in the Bat Cave area above Caballo Lake, near Truth or Consequences, just right of Trojan Wall. Its ten routes are mainly sport, with one trad line, and the lines are shorter, lower angle and easier than those on the neighboring Super Hero Wall, mostly 5.7 to 5.10. Limestone here is solid and sharp, with small features and huecos. The wall faces south and gets sun from late morning until sunset, since the mountain to the east blocks the early light. A few lines go for multiple pitches.
